body:
> Found piloting hkb on `french-tech-homies/pipao-v2` on 2026-08-27/28.

## Why

`src/context.js:87` renders the task's `kb.skills` into the worker brief:

```js
if (task.kb.skills?.length) lines.push(`Skills to apply: ${task.kb.skills.map((s) => '`/' + s + '`').join(', ')}\n`);
```

But `Skill` is not in `DEFAULT_PROFILES`' `CLAUDE_TOOLS` (`src/board.js`), and workers launch `--permission-mode dontAsk`, which **denies** an unlisted tool rather than prompting. So setting `kb.skills` tells the worker to invoke something it is guaranteed to be refused.

That is worse than the field not existing: the worker reads an instruction from its own brief, tries it, is denied, and has to decide whether the instruction or the denial is authoritative. `--skills` is advertised in `hkb create`'s usage line and in the MCP schema ("Skills the worker should load"), so the field reads as a capability grant. It is not one.

Verified on this board: `profiles.claude.allowed_tools` contains no `Skill` entry, and a worker's own transcript shows the equivalent denial for an MCP tool —

```
Permission to use mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp has been denied
because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode.
```

## What

Pick one, or both:

1. **Add `Skill` to `CLAUDE_TOOLS`** in `src/board.js`, so the field grants what it advertises. Skills are repo-local and already reachable with `Read`, so this widens very little.
2. **Have `doctor` warn** when any task sets `kb.skills` while its profile's `allowed_tools` lacks `Skill` — needed regardless for boards whose profiles were written before the fix.

Worth deciding at the same time whether `kb.skills` should *inject* the tool into that task's launch rather than relying on the profile, since the field is per-task and the allowlist is per-profile.

## Done when

- [ ] A task with `kb.skills` set can actually invoke the named skill under `dontAsk`.
- [ ] `hkb doctor` flags the mismatch on a board where it exists.
- [ ] `hkb create --skills` usage text says whether it grants or merely suggests.
goal: A task with kb.skills set can invoke the named skill under dontAsk, or doctor flags the mismatch; the --skills usage text says whether it grants or suggests.
title: kb.skills tells the worker to use a Skill tool the default profile denies
